- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend, but true outcomes often spike higher in the middle or end of the period, suggesting lag in capturing sudden price surges.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., 86+), model forecasts overshoot and then gradually decay — indicating overreaction to short-term volatility.
- Mean reversion is evident: forecasts tend to be higher than true values in the first 10–15 days, then converge downward, suggesting model overweights recent trends.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the latter half of the 30-day window — true prices often dip below forecasted levels after mid-period.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; true outcomes show more volatility, especially in the first 10 days, suggesting model suppresses noise or ignores short-term shocks.
- When true prices are above 85, model tends to overestimate — but when below 80, it underestimates, indicating asymmetric bias toward higher prices.
- Model exhibits “late correction” — true values often dip below forecast in the last 5–7 days, suggesting model doesn’t adjust for tail risks or policy-driven corrections.
